runs.meaning: tests/linkedin-lead-forms.test.mjs against a build of e45400e: expected red, 0/8 pass (WRITE_CONTRACT_UNAVAILABLE for creation; lead form reads blocked by account scope)
85 related suites in the worktree before assembly: 1236/1236 pass

development_failures: One new test failed on its first run because it read the native read result at the wrong level (data.id instead of data.data.id); the test was corrected, not the code.

Design review found that LinkedIn documents 19-digit lead form IDs, beyond JavaScript safe integers, so responses from /rest/leadForms now keep such integers as exact source text; and that the spending word heuristic would ask for spending confirmation when question text mentions budgets, so lead form creation is excluded from it.
A first draft placed the account state read inside the TikTok branch of snapshotPlans, where LinkedIn never reaches it; this was caught while reviewing the edit, before any test run, and moved.
limitations: Synthetic validation only; no live provider credentials, reads or account mutations in this batch.
LinkedIn documents the created form ID in x-restli-id without an example value, so both a bare numeric ID and a urn:li:leadGenForm URN are accepted.
state DRAFT is required because LinkedIn documents it in the creation example although the schema marks state read-only; a different read-back state is reported as inconclusive.
Server-side normalization of URLs or text, if any, is reported as inconclusive rather than verified.
Limits the docs do not state (name, headline and question lengths, number of questions) are left to LinkedIn; review bounds the request at 64 KiB.
Lead gen creatives are not yet required to reference owned forms; this is a P2 follow-up in the handoff.
No GitHub CLI here and CAMCP is private: CI for the pushed commits was not read from this checkout.
No local Docker; container build/smoke evidence comes from GitHub Actions on the pushed commit.
